answer: One workable design: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because kernel only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, voyage is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any garden approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
